name: Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy
aliases: X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy

criteria.description: Presence of expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat (>38 repeats) in the androgen receptor gene
Progressive lower motor neuron signs including muscle weakness, atrophy, and fasciculations predominantly in bulbar and limb muscles
Signs of androgen insensitivity such as gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, and reduced fertility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Genetic confirmation of expanded CAG repeat in androgen receptor gene plus clinical evidence of lower motor neuron involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electromyography and family history support diagnosis but are not mandatory

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate)
Hormonal abnormalities including elevated luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone
imaging: Muscle MRI showing atrophy and fatty infiltration
Brain MRI usually normal or nonspecific
other: Electromyography showing chronic denervation and reinnervation
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating mild sensory neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Predominant spasticity rather than lower motor neuron signs

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness with upper motor neuron signs
Absence of androgen insensitivity signs in a male with suspected diagnosis
Family history inconsistent with X-linked inheritance
references: Kennedy WR, Alter M, Sung JH. Progressive proximal spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy of late onset. A sex-linked recessive trait. Neurology. 1968.
La Spada AR, Wilson EM, Lubahn DB, Harding AE, Fischbeck KH. Androgen receptor gene mutations in X-linked spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy. Nature. 1991.
Orphanet: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (Kennedy disease).
